profile.entities: 3B India (standalone open-kit MDx); TRUPCR Europe (UK sub); Coris BioConcept (Belgium, acquired Aug 2024, AMR rapid diagnostics). No "Kilpest" parent — Kilpest WAS the company, now renamed.
profile.mgmt: Mr. Dhirendra Dubey (Chairman & MD); Mr. Nikhil Dubey (Whole-Time Director); plus unnamed finance "Management" voice. Hosted by Nuvama (Ranvir Singh).
profile.subseg: PCR / real-time molecular kits; oncology & genetic assays; AMR rapid diagnostics; export (TRUPCR Europe); domestic open-kit
profile.themes: Import-substitution / Make-in-India molecular diagnostics (India open-kit replacing imported sample-to-answer); US FDA market-access optionality (AMR).

bull_bear.body:
- ~INR230 cr cash/treasury; generating ~INR40 cr+ FCF/yr → recurring "cash pile" problem.
- M&A budget ~INR140 cr flagged earlier; 3-4 consultants engaged (France, UK, US); "few advanced discussions," expect "something by year-end" (Q1/Q2 unlikely). Target by year-end FY27.
- M&A criteria: topline ≥EUR2 m, growing sector, EBITDA-positive OR turnaround; broadening beyond hardcore IVD into adjacent diagnostics/molecular/genetics. Preferred multiples 6-8x vs sellers asking ~20x (valuation gap = key blocker).
- Treasury mix: ~5-7% equity MF; ~30-35% FDs; ~30-35% treasury bonds; rest AAA corporate bonds (e.g., Tata Capital). Liquidatable within 3-4 days; FDs/bonds laddered to mature.
- Plan to keep ~INR50 cr permanent reserve, deploy rest into M&A. Tax: Coris carry-forward EUR2-3 m → ~3-4 yrs no Coris tax.
bull_bear.title: Capital Allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Domestic growth slowed to ~2-3% YoY last two quarters (post high FY24/25 base + FY25 flu/dengue exceptional INR4.2 cr).
- Chinese low-cost competition in high-volume respiratory/Entero rapid tests (hits ~23% of Coris non-AMR mix).
- Middle East geopolitical tension hit some export markets in FY26.
- US FDA timeline uncertainty (could slip beyond 1.5 yrs).
- HAT order is lumpy, Congo-specific, Ebola-exposed; one-time PAT contributor that fades.
- Coris H1 FY27 EBITDA losses; consolidation of unprofitable quarters drags reported H1.
- M&A execution risk — valuation gap (sellers at 20x).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, candid, detailed on numbers. Repeatedly refused QoQ analysis ("quarter-on-quarter is very difficult"), pushing full-year framing — partly to deflect the soft domestic last-2-quarter trend. Transparent on one-offs (HAT, R&D amortisation, flu/dengue base). Disciplined on M&A valuation ("won't overpay at 20x"). Mildly impatient with investor's heavy arithmetic but cooperative.
bull_bear.title: Management Tone

bull_bear.body:
- The INR60 cr consolidated PAT is flattered by Coris's HAT order landing in the consolidated (profitable) 7-month window — sustainable Coris is barely EBITDA-positive.
- "Only two earnings calls/year" going forward reduces disclosure cadence — watch for less granularity.
- Renaming Kilpest → 3B BlackBio Dx completes identity shift to pure diagnostics.
- Real moat = IVDR + (pending) US FDA as regulatory barriers that keep Chinese volume players out of AMR/oncology/high-panel niches.
- Pricing chain: kit sold to distributor ~INR700-800 → hospital buys ~INR1,000 → end test billed ~INR2,000-2,500.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious Insights

bull_bear.body:
- M&A is one of four stated strategic priorities; the company is "actively looking for M&A opportunities across globe preferably in the EU and the USA", targeting manufacturers or distributors in molecular, microbiology, immunology and similar IVD segments.
- Acquisition discipline is explicit: over the last 2 years several IVD companies were evaluated but valuations were high on the back of Covid profits and "the Sales & EBITDA were not matching our IRR or future growth possibility, hence we did not proceed".
- Funds will also be deployed into the joint venture created in Manchester, UK "depending on the need"; the Coris deal is framed as strengthening credibility "as a genuine buyer".
- Working capital is being run loose by design - a liberal credit policy to avoid losing customers to post-COVID competition results in "higher debtor level currently which we will gradually bring down in the coming years" - while the agro business "operates with minimal debt".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **3B India (open-kit MDx):** ~INR86.5 cr; dominant in oncology & higher multi-panels (respiratory, meningitis); ~15% share of INR500-600 cr Indian addressable market. Capacity utilisation only ~50%.
- **TRUPCR Europe (UK):** INR20.67 cr, ~40% 4-yr CAGR; faces competition but managing.
- **Coris (Belgium, AMR rapid diagnostics):** ~INR50 cr annualised; AMR is growth/margin driver; ~23% of remaining (non-AMR: respiratory, Entero) under Chinese low-price pressure; HAT contract = EUR6 m total (2024, 4-yr), ~EUR3.45 m executed, ~EUR2.4 m remaining through FY28 (Congo-specific, Ebola risk to timing).
business.title: Segment Detail

business.body:
- *Challenge:* Chinese low-cost respiratory/rapid-test glut pressures commodity assays → *beneficiary tilt:* AMR/oncology/high-panel niche players (3B/Coris) with regulatory moats (IVDR/FDA). ✅ self-beneficiary via menu mix-shift to AMR.
- *Challenge:* US AMR market import-dependent, FDA-gated → ⭐ optionality beneficiary = Coris Resist-5 on clearance (INR100 cr market, currently served by a French exporter via FDA-registered US distributor).
- Beneficiaries (external listed names): none clearly identified.

---
business.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries

business.body:
- Describes itself as a "well established molecular diagnostics (MDx) brand with largest range of Indian IVD and CE-IVD Products available", with 120+ molecular diagnostic assays developed and over 40 key assays CE-IVD marked post the new IVDR regulations.
- Claims to be the "only company to have qPCR Assays, Lateral Flow Tests and NGS assays available together" and the "only molecular company globally to integrate offerings for Rapid Diagnostics (Lateral Flow) & NGS solutions".
- Estimates the India MDx Total Addressable Market at approx. Rs 500-600 Cr and claims approximately 15% market share, "positioning us among the market leaders".
- Reach cited as product and customer support access to over 1,000 labs / hospitals in India across 100+ cities, plus 70+ countries and 200+ customers internationally across Europe, Middle East, APAC, LATAM and North America.
- Differentiators listed include being "the only Indian Company to have a subsidiary in UK", the only Indian company to get US FDA (EUA) for COVID in 2020, and both India and UK sites ISO 13485 certified by BSI, UK; Coris is described as "synonymous to AMR in the global market and a respected European brand".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Coris BioConcept SRL, Belgium was acquired on 29th August 2025; under Ind AS consolidation runs only from the acquisition date, so this is the first year Q1 numbers are consolidated versus a non-consolidated prior year.
- [Contract] Coris holds a Belgium Government HAT order (test for the parasite causing African sleeping sickness) of EUR 6.0M received in February 2024 to be supplied over 4 years; a EUR 1.41M HAT order was recently confirmed for supply in Q3 (December 2026) versus EUR 1.35M supplied in December 2025. Coris earnings are seasonal - Q1 and Q2 loss-making, Q3 and Q4 profitable on HAT supply.
- [Regulation] EU IVDR (Regulation 2017/746) applies from 26 May 2026; the company can continue selling as legacy devices until 31 December 2028 (transition period), by which time IVDR certifications are expected.
- [Segment mix / risk] Within Coris, AMR grew 12% and is 70% of sales, while the remaining 30% de-grew 54% "because of Chinese competition"; geopolitical tensions are repeatedly cited as delaying or cancelling export orders and complicating logistics.
- [Legacy division] The agrochemicals division is run for stability, not growth - focused on GeM electronic government tenders for vector-borne disease control, exports mainly to Bangladesh, and supply to old customers - with an existing catalogue spanning chemicals (insecticides 70, fungicides 15, herbicides 11, public health 11) and biologicals (bio pesticide 07, health & hygiene 06, bio fertilizers 05).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- 3B standalone structurally ~55% EBITDA / ~60% GM — niche molecular = high margin.
- Consolidated margin dragged to ~40% by Coris (~10% EBITDA) + TRUPCR (~15-20%).
- Coris EBITDA depressed by high employee cost / large team; mgmt rationalising product costing toward 10% EBITDA over 1-2 yrs.
- Q4 is the new cost baseline (full Coris + TRUPCR + 3B consolidation; employee & other expenses up 3-4x YoY on Coris).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & Cost

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this call):** First call reflecting FULL consolidation of Coris (7 mo) + TRUPCR + 3B. Consol rev ~INR142 cr, PAT ~INR60 cr. Guidance FY27: 15-20% rev & EBITDA growth; topline build to ~INR175-180 cr. Coris EBITDA-flat FY27, 10% by FY28-29. US FDA (Resist-5) targeted FY28. IVDR QMS audits done (BSI). Sample-to-answer OEM installs from Q3 FY27. ~INR230 cr treasury, M&A "by year-end." Cadence cut to 2 calls/yr.
- *(Prior quarters referenced by mgmt: sample-to-answer & POC mentioned last call; M&A candidates met in Dubai; competition commentary unchanged QoQ. No structured prior note on file.)*
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth: 15-20% for FY27** (consolidated, all businesses) — reiterated multiple times, incl closing remarks.
- **EBITDA growth: also 15-20%** ("same pace"); margin profile to "remain similar" — no major erosion expected on 3B.
- **Blended FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other-income): ~40-45%** (investor-built, mgmt said "hopefully"). 3B+TRUPCR EBITDA INR69.22 cr → grow ~15% → ~INR79 cr.
- **FY27 topline build (investor-confirmed by mgmt):** 3B+TRUPCR ~INR107 cr → ~INR124-125 cr; Coris ~INR36 cr (7-mo) → ~INR52 cr (full yr); total ~INR175-180 cr.
- **Coris EBITDA: FY27 "slight EBITDA positive" (flat); 5-7% in FY28; ~10% by FY28-29.** FY27 Q1 & Q2 will be LOSS-making (HAT order books in H2 / advance only).
- **Depreciation FY27: ~INR4.5-5 cr** (similar to FY26).
- **Segment split of growth:** domestic ~15% (only ~20% if seasonal flu/dengue spike), exports ~20-25%.
- **Cadence change:** only TWO earnings calls/year going forward (half-yearly).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)

outlook.body:
- **US FDA submission for Coris AMR** — lead product **Resist-5 / Carba5** (carbapenemase resistance panel), ~30-35% of Coris revenue; targeted FY28 opportunity. Lab tie-ups for clinical trials done; mgmt "confident" but timeline 1–1.5 yrs+ ("will definitely happen, only timing"). US rapid-AMR market ~INR100 cr / 10 m EUR. US could become ~20% of Coris revenue → 1-1.5 m EUR (INR11-16 cr), offsetting HAT runoff.
- **IVDR transition** (EU) — BSI appointed as notified body; IVDR-aligned QMS audits completed; technical documentation review for key product families progressing. Seen as a competitive moat / barrier to Chinese imports.
- **Sample-to-answer system** — via OEM (not in-house dev); validation ongoing, "initial results good"; expect 2-3 lab installs from Q3 FY27 onward (already baked into 15-20% guidance).
outlook.title: Pipeline (new assays / regulatory approvals)

outlook.body:
- Oncology & genetic high-panel menu (pricing power; competition only from MNCs, no erosion).
- Export expansion: Europe, Africa, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, Latin America; "lot of market where we are not present."
- US FDA = largest lever (US = ~50% of global MDx; currently absent).
- M&A roll-up funded by ~INR230 cr treasury (see §9).
- Sample-to-answer (OEM) opens the ~30-35% of Indian market currently outside open-kit.
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: Niche, high-margin (≈55% standalone EBITDA) Indian molecular-diagnostics open-kit maker compounding ~15% domestic / ~20-25% export, now adding inorganic legs (TRUPCR Europe ~40% CAGR, Coris AMR in Belgium) funded by a ~INR230 cr cash/treasury war-chest earmarked for further M&A; key optionality = US FDA clearance for Coris AMR (Resist-5/Carba5) opening the largest global MDx market.

- Export expansion: Europe, Africa, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, Latin America; "lot of market where we are not present."
- US FDA = largest lever (US = ~50% of global MDx; currently absent).
- M&A roll-up funded by ~INR230 cr treasury (see §9).
- Sample-to-answer (OEM) opens the ~30-35% of Indian market currently outside open-kit.

margins.title: Margins & Cost
margins.body:
- 3B standalone structurally ~55% EBITDA / ~60% GM — niche molecular = high margin.
- Consolidated margin dragged to ~40% by Coris (~10% EBITDA) + TRUPCR (~15-20%).
- Coris EBITDA depressed by high employee cost / large team; mgmt rationalising product costing toward 10% EBITDA over 1-2 yrs.
- Q4 is the new cost baseline (full Coris + TRUPCR + 3B consolidation; employee & other expenses up 3-4x YoY on Coris).

capital_allocation.title: Capital Allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- ~INR230 cr cash/treasury; generating ~INR40 cr+ FCF/yr → recurring "cash pile" problem.
- M&A budget ~INR140 cr flagged earlier; 3-4 consultants engaged (France, UK, US); "few advanced discussions," expect "something by year-end" (Q1/Q2 unlikely). Target by year-end FY27.
- M&A criteria: topline ≥EUR2 m, growing sector, EBITDA-positive OR turnaround; broadening beyond hardcore IVD into adjacent diagnostics/molecular/genetics. Preferred multiples 6-8x vs sellers asking ~20x (valuation gap = key blocker).
- Treasury mix: ~5-7% equity MF; ~30-35% FDs; ~30-35% treasury bonds; rest AAA corporate bonds (e.g., Tata Capital). Liquidatable within 3-4 days; FDs/bonds laddered to mature.
- Plan to keep ~INR50 cr permanent reserve, deploy rest into M&A. Tax: Coris carry-forward EUR2-3 m → ~3-4 yrs no Coris tax.

management_tone.title: Management Tone
management_tone.body: Confident, candid, detailed on numbers. Repeatedly refused QoQ analysis ("quarter-on-quarter is very difficult"), pushing full-year framing — partly to deflect the soft domestic last-2-quarter trend. Transparent on one-offs (HAT, R&D amortisation, flu/dengue base). Disciplined on M&A valuation ("won't overpay at 20x"). Mildly impatient with investor's heavy arithmetic but cooperative.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Domestic growth slowed to ~2-3% YoY last two quarters (post high FY24/25 base + FY25 flu/dengue exceptional INR4.2 cr).
- Chinese low-cost competition in high-volume respiratory/Entero rapid tests (hits ~23% of Coris non-AMR mix).
- Middle East geopolitical tension hit some export markets in FY26.
- US FDA timeline uncertainty (could slip beyond 1.5 yrs).
- HAT order is lumpy, Congo-specific, Ebola-exposed; one-time PAT contributor that fades.
- Coris H1 FY27 EBITDA losses; consolidation of unprofitable quarters drags reported H1.
- M&A execution risk — valuation gap (sellers at 20x).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious Insights
non_obvious.body:
- The INR60 cr consolidated PAT is flattered by Coris's HAT order landing in the consolidated (profitable) 7-month window — sustainable Coris is barely EBITDA-positive.
- "Only two earnings calls/year" going forward reduces disclosure cadence — watch for less granularity.
- Renaming Kilpest → 3B BlackBio Dx completes identity shift to pure diagnostics.
- Real moat = IVDR + (pending) US FDA as regulatory barriers that keep Chinese volume players out of AMR/oncology/high-panel niches.
- Pricing chain: kit sold to distributor ~INR700-800 → hospital buys ~INR1,000 → end test billed ~INR2,000-2,500.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- *Challenge:* Chinese low-cost respiratory/rapid-test glut pressures commodity assays → *beneficiary tilt:* AMR/oncology/high-panel niche players (3B/Coris) with regulatory moats (IVDR/FDA). ✅ self-beneficiary via menu mix-shift to AMR.
- *Challenge:* US AMR market import-dependent, FDA-gated → ⭐ optionality beneficiary = Coris Resist-5 on clearance (INR100 cr market, currently served by a French exporter via FDA-registered US distributor).
- Beneficiaries (external listed names): none clearly identified.

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this call):** First call reflecting FULL consolidation of Coris (7 mo) + TRUPCR + 3B. Consol rev ~INR142 cr, PAT ~INR60 cr. Guidance FY27: 15-20% rev & EBITDA growth; topline build to ~INR175-180 cr. Coris EBITDA-flat FY27, 10% by FY28-29. US FDA (Resist-5) targeted FY28. IVDR QMS audits done (BSI). Sample-to-answer OEM installs from Q3 FY27. ~INR230 cr treasury, M&A "by year-end." Cadence cut to 2 calls/yr.
- *(Prior quarters referenced by mgmt: sample-to-answer & POC mentioned last call; M&A candidates met in Dubai; competition commentary unchanged QoQ. No structured prior note on file.)*

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Coris BioConcept SRL, Belgium was acquired on 29th August 2025; under Ind AS consolidation runs only from the acquisition date, so this is the first year Q1 numbers are consolidated versus a non-consolidated prior year.
- [Contract] Coris holds a Belgium Government HAT order (test for the parasite causing African sleeping sickness) of EUR 6.0M received in February 2024 to be supplied over 4 years; a EUR 1.41M HAT order was recently confirmed for supply in Q3 (December 2026) versus EUR 1.35M supplied in December 2025. Coris earnings are seasonal - Q1 and Q2 loss-making, Q3 and Q4 profitable on HAT supply.
- [Regulation] EU IVDR (Regulation 2017/746) applies from 26 May 2026; the company can continue selling as legacy devices until 31 December 2028 (transition period), by which time IVDR certifications are expected.
- [Segment mix / risk] Within Coris, AMR grew 12% and is 70% of sales, while the remaining 30% de-grew 54% "because of Chinese competition"; geopolitical tensions are repeatedly cited as delaying or cancelling export orders and complicating logistics.
- [Legacy division] The agrochemicals division is run for stability, not growth - focused on GeM electronic government tenders for vector-borne disease control, exports mainly to Bangladesh, and supply to old customers - with an existing catalogue spanning chemicals (insecticides 70, fungicides 15, herbicides 11, public health 11) and biologicals (bio pesticide 07, health & hygiene 06, bio fertilizers 05).

- **Revenue growth: 15-20% for FY27** (consolidated, all businesses) — reiterated multiple times, incl closing remarks.
- **EBITDA growth: also 15-20%** ("same pace"); margin profile to "remain similar" — no major erosion expected on 3B.
- **Blended FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other-income): ~40-45%** (investor-built, mgmt said "hopefully"). 3B+TRUPCR EBITDA INR69.22 cr → grow ~15% → ~INR79 cr.
- **FY27 topline build (investor-confirmed by mgmt):** 3B+TRUPCR ~INR107 cr → ~INR124-125 cr; Coris ~INR36 cr (7-mo) → ~INR52 cr (full yr); total ~INR175-180 cr.
- **Coris EBITDA: FY27 "slight EBITDA positive" (flat); 5-7% in FY28; ~10% by FY28-29.** FY27 Q1 & Q2 will be LOSS-making (HAT order books in H2 / advance only).
- **Depreciation FY27: ~INR4.5-5 cr** (similar to FY26).
- **Segment split of growth:** domestic ~15% (only ~20% if seasonal flu/dengue spike), exports ~20-25%.
- **Cadence change:** only TWO earnings calls/year going forward (half-yearly).
pipeline (new assays / regulatory approv:
- **US FDA submission for Coris AMR** — lead product **Resist-5 / Carba5** (carbapenemase resistance panel), ~30-35% of Coris revenue; targeted FY28 opportunity. Lab tie-ups for clinical trials done; mgmt "confident" but timeline 1–1.5 yrs+ ("will definitely happen, only timing"). US rapid-AMR market ~INR100 cr / 10 m EUR. US could become ~20% of Coris revenue → 1-1.5 m EUR (INR11-16 cr), offsetting HAT runoff.
- **IVDR transition** (EU) — BSI appointed as notified body; IVDR-aligned QMS audits completed; technical documentation review for key product families progressing. Seen as a competitive moat / barrier to Chinese imports.
